body:
## Problem

The reviewer leaf is asked to independently reproduce every recorded gate green, but the gate runner scripts the frozen gate records name (`./engine/scripts/run-docs-check.sh`, `./engine/scripts/run-suite.sh` in the pdca-pdca instance) are **absent from the reviewer's permitted target checkout**. The reviewer can only fall back to approximations (direct `unittest discover`, local whitespace checks) and must escalate the discrepancy.

Evidence from the pdca-pdca instance's 2026-08-01 Act review — **4 of 9** frozen bundles (cycles for #331, #341, #368, #375) carried §6 items of the form *"the declared oracle `./engine/scripts/run-*.sh` is absent in this review directory, so the recorded pass cannot be independently reproduced"*.

## Underlying gap: no sandbox-interior preflight

`pdca doctor` checks the **host**, not the leaf sandbox interior. Gate additions (copier, docs runner, engine scripts) silently drift out of sandbox seeding — same class as #161/#163 (and #276/#277 for the network layer). Nothing catches the drift until a reviewer hits the wall mid-cycle, as issue_375's §10 recorded: *"No preflight identifies leaf-sandbox dependency gaps — doctor checks the host, not the sandbox interior."*

## Proposal (either or both)

- **Seed the oracles:** include the gate-runner scripts (and the inputs they need) in the reviewer's permitted target, so a recorded green is mechanically re-runnable at Check;
- **Sandbox-interior preflight:** a doctor mode (or per-gate declaration) that verifies each gate's declared command resolves *inside* the leaf sandbox — alternatively a per-gate `reviewer_reproducible` declaration so the matrix is honest about what the reviewer can and cannot rerun.

## Origin

Filed from the pdca-pdca self-hosting instance's Act review (process/act-log.md, 2026-08-01) — recurring-signal routing (4 of 9 frozen cycles), nominated explicitly by bundle issue_375 §10. Sibling reports from the same review: #401, #402.

comments.body:
Further evidence from the 2026-08-02 Act review of the pdca-pdca instance — with a sharper diagnosis than "the oracles are absent".

The gate wrappers are **present**, at the instance root (`engine/scripts/run-docs-check.sh`, `run-suite.sh`, `run-verify.sh`). They are also written to be run *from* that root with `$PDCA_WORKTREE` set — both scripts open with `WT="${PDCA_WORKTREE:?worktree isolation must be on}"` and resolve `$(pwd)/.venv/bin/python3`. The reviewer, however, works from `$PDCA_TARGET` (the target checkout), where no `engine/scripts/` exists and `PDCA_WORKTREE` is unset. So it reports the oracle "absent" and escalates.

Two consequences worth folding into this issue:

- It is a **reachability + invocation-contract** gap, not only a seeding gap. Copying the scripts into the sandbox would not be enough; the reviewer also needs the cwd and `PDCA_WORKTREE`/venv contract the wrapper was written against.
- It is **intermittent**, which is the strongest hint that guidance (not machinery) is the missing piece: across the four most recent frozen bundles the T2/T3 rows cleared on `issue_356` and escalated on `issue_380`, `issue_386`, `issue_387` — same instance, same gates, same wrappers, different reviewer behaviour.

Recorded as an Act candidate in `results/issue_386/SUMMARY.md` §10: "Reviewer re-runs gates from `$PDCA_TARGET` instead of the instance root with `PDCA_WORKTREE=`, so T2/T3/T4 land as NEEDS-HUMAN (cleared on 356, not on 380/386/387)."

title: Reviewer sandbox lacks the T2/T3 gate oracles and no preflight detects it — recorded greens are unreproducible, recurring as NEEDS-HUMAN
